items.title: Mozambique: Niassa discusses local development strategies
items.summary: It is in this context that Niassa is holding its second Development Observatory for the current year, a consultative and participatory forum bringing together the Government and national and foreign partners to discuss strategies for promoting sustainable socio-economic development, with a focus on planning and budgeting, as well as monitoring and evaluating government instruments At the opening of the event, the provincial governor, Judite Massengele, called on the private sector to increase investment in agriculture, agro-industry, marketing and other economic activities capable of creating jobs, stimulating the local economy and adding value to the province’s production “We reiterate our commitment to participatory, transparent and results-oriented governance, valuing the contributions of this Observatory and ensuring that they are duly followed up, within the scope of institutional responsibilities and available resources,” Massengele said The provincial government expects the strategies and recommendations resulting from the meeting to help increase production and productivity…

items.title: Mozambique: Central bank forecasts rising cost of living in early 2027
items.summary: The warning was issued on Wednesday by Bank of Mozambique Governor Felisberto Navalha during the opening of the institution’s 51st Consultative Council, being held in Tete province. “With regard to prices, we anticipate some pressure in the short term and a slowdown in the medium term,” Navalha said According to the central bank governor, domestic factors behind the rising cost of living include uncertainties over the scale of imported inflation, the evolution of public debt and government arrears, as well as the impact of climate shocks, particularly the El Niño phenomenon. “Externally, there are uncertainties about the duration and magnitude of the effects of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Europe on international trade flows, the global supply of goods, and international fuel and food prices,” Navalha added Should these scenarios continue to worsen, the Bank of Mozambique says it may reverse its current monetary policy stance.

items.title: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems amid war in Tigray
items.summary: The acquisition of fighter jets comes amid ongoing tensions with Eritrea Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia, as fighting intensified in the northern Tigray region neighbouring Eritrea Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who is attending the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, described the acquisition as a "milestone" that would boost Ethiopia's defence capacity He said Ethiopia and Russia agreed on the deal several years ago and the warplanes had come ahead of schedule. He also said that Ethiopia had plans to acquire four S-400 air defence systems from Moscow The Ethiopian leader said the military hardware was essential to protect the country from external threats Abiy, who described Russian President Vladimir Putin, "as a close friend of Ethiopia", said Ethiopia had now become the first country in sub‑Saharan Africa to own this kind of "advanced combat technology." "If we fail to build this capability, surviving as a country in our region will become difficult.

items.title: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over DR Congo conflict
items.summary: Eastern DR Congo has been plagued by conflict with M23 recapturing Goma and then Bukavu in early 2025 The United States has imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its alleged support for the M23 rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing pressure on Kigali to withdraw its troops and halt support for the rebels "Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said The sanctions come months after Rwanda and DR Congo signed a US-brokered peace agreement aimed at ending the conflict Fighting has continued in eastern DR Congo since early 2025, when M23 seized the cities of Goma and Bukavu. Rwanda denies backing M23 The US Treasury says Rwanda's defence ministry directed thousands of troops to fight alongside M23 in eastern DR Congo, providing weapons, equipment, logistics and training The M23 has seized mineral-rich areas, including gold-mining sites in South Kivu and Rubaya, a major coltan-producing area in North Kivu.

items.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
items.summary: Neither Gadi Eisenkot (left) or Benjamin Netanyahu (right) are projected to win enough seats for a majority Israel looks to be in political deadlock With more than 90% of votes counted after Tuesday's election, neither the incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, nor the bloc of his key challenger Gadi Eisenkot look set to win a majority In order to form a government, it looks likely one of the leading parties would have to break their campaign promises - meaning the most probable outcome may well be new elections Could Netanyahu persuade Eisenkot to join him in a national unity government? Eisenkot would have to abandon his key platform to do so.
